meta.description: Runs the MS-DIAL preprocessing workflow (peak picking, MS2Dec spectral deconvolution, alignment, gap-filling) and imports the alignment-result table into R or Python with honest filtering. Use when preprocessing LC-MS DDA/DIA (SWATH) raw data with MS-DIAL, deciding MS-DIAL vs XCMS, configuring the MsdialConsoleApp console run, or parsing an MS-DIAL export into a clean feature matrix.

scientific_integrity.detail: All cited literature (Tsugawa 2015/2020/2024, Li 2018, Mahieu 2017, Broadhurst 2018, Stein 1999) are real, correctly attributed papers; no fabricated DOIs, PMIDs, sample sizes or effect sizes in any of the 5 outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Preprocessing pipeline for aggregate metabolomics data; no individual-subject diagnostic or prescriptive content in any output.

methodological_ground.detail: No methodological fallacies observed; correctly warns that a marker list surviving only one preprocessing pipeline is a candidate not a result, and correctly defers QC-CV/D-ratio/imputation to normalization-qc rather than reimplementing them inline.

code_usability.detail: The R and Python parsing/filtering code the Skill actually supplies ran correctly on independently-generated synthetic exports (verified against ground truth in Inputs 1 and 4). The CLI-naming and GC-MS-exclusion defects found are documentation/version-currency errors, not unrunnable code, so M4 is not triggered; they are recorded as P1 recommendations instead.

functional_suitability.note: Broad, real coverage (decision framework, console run, R/Python import, honest filtering, failure modes), but the core 'Run MS-DIAL Headless' commands (MsdialConsoleApp lcmsdda/lcmsdia) do not match the installed MS-DIAL 5.5.260820 console, and the central 'MS-DIAL 5 excludes GC-MS' claim is contradicted by that same installed release.

reliability.note: Common Errors table is genuinely useful (header offset, ABF-only DIA input, version drift) and the Version Compatibility section builds in a verify-before-trust habit; it does not, however, warn about the pandas TRUE/FALSE auto-bool-cast trap found in Input 4.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md (~210 lines) and usage-guide.md are both concise for the scope covered; one small, on-topic example script.

agent_usability.note: Clear trigger description, well-enumerated workflow, and a strong decision-tree table; docked for internal inconsistency between the commands it tells the agent to run and the verification step it also tells the agent to run.

human_usability.note: Well-organized with worked examples and a references section; no explicit 'When NOT to use' section (routing to XCMS/normalization-qc/metabolite-annotation substitutes for it, imperfectly).

security.note: No credential handling, no eval/exec of raw strings, no destructive operations; all local file parsing.

maintainability.note: Well-modularized sections and real, checkable citations; the shipped example script runs correctly (verified), but the CLI command examples show the Skill was not re-validated against a current MS-DIAL release.

agent_specific.note: Good trigger precision and composability (explicit Related Skills cross-references to xcms-preprocessing, lipidomics, metabolite-annotation, normalization-qc); the Version Compatibility section is a genuine escape hatch even though the specific names it tells the agent to check are themselves wrong.

inputs.label: Build DDA console command, import AlignResult into R, filter honestly
inputs.note: R import+filter code (run verbatim from SKILL.md) is fully correct on a real synthetic export; the documented MsdialConsoleApp lcmsdda command does not match the installed console.

assertions.text: The documented 'MsdialConsoleApp lcmsdda -i ... -o ... -m ...' command runs against the installed MS-DIAL console as written
assertions.note: Executed: the real binary is MSDIALCUI.exe and its help banner lists no 'lcmsdda' command; only 'lcms' exists for LC-MS (verified via `MSDIALCUI.exe` with no args and `MSDIALCUI.exe lcms --help`).

assertions.text: The Skill instructs verifying the installed console's real subcommands before trusting the documented command
assertions.note: Version Compatibility section explicitly says to run the console with no arguments first.

assertions.text: R import code correctly splits metadata columns from per-sample intensity columns on a real 4-header-row MS-DIAL-style export
assertions.note: Executed: 45/45 rows and 10/10 sample columns recovered exactly, matching the synthetic ground truth.

assertions.text: Fill% >= 70 filter keeps only features whose real Fill% truly meets the threshold
assertions.note: Executed: programmatic ground-truth check confirmed TRUE for all 15 retained features.

assertions.text: Output excludes gap-filled/low-confidence features before they could be treated as measurements
assertions.note: Filtered table contains only the 15/45 features with Fill% >= 70, as the Skill intends.

inputs.label: DIA/SWATH console command and ABF input requirement
inputs.note: Same lcmsdia-does-not-exist defect as Input 1; the Skill also never explains that DDA vs DIA is actually selected via the -m method file, not a console token.

assertions.text: Documented 'lcmsdia' console token exists in the installed MS-DIAL console
assertions.note: Executed: help banner and MSDIALCUI.exe lcms --help confirm only 'lcms' exists; no separate DIA token.

assertions.text: Skill correctly explains that DIA requires ABF-format input, not mzML
assertions.note: Documented and consistent with MS-DIAL's known ABF-only DIA constraint; not contradicted by anything found in the console help (which has no input-format flag to check against).

assertions.text: Skill correctly explains why DIA/SWATH needs MS2Dec deconvolution (chimeric spectra)
assertions.note: Prose explanation is accurate and consistent with the MS-DIAL literature (Tsugawa 2015).

assertions.text: SKILL.md documents how DDA vs DIA is actually distinguished in the real console (method-file parameter, not a separate subcommand)
assertions.note: Not documented anywhere in SKILL.md; the real console exposes one 'lcms' command for both, so an agent following the Skill has no path to the correct invocation.

inputs.label: GC-EI data on MS-DIAL 5 -- is GC-MS supported?
inputs.note: The Skill's central claim that MS-DIAL 5 excludes GC-MS is contradicted by the installed 5.5.260820 console, which ships a working 'gcms' subcommand and its own MsdialGcMsApi.dll.

assertions.text: SKILL.md's claim 'MS-DIAL 5-alpha excludes GC-MS' / 'No GC-MS option in MS-DIAL 5' holds for the installed, current MS-DIAL 5 console
assertions.note: Executed: MSDIALCUI.exe (v5.5.260820) lists 'gcms' as a real subcommand and `gcms --help` prints a full, working -i/-o/-m option list; MsdialGcMsApi.dll ships in the same release.

assertions.text: Skill correctly explains why GC-EI deconvolution is fundamentally different from LC peak-picking
assertions.note: Accurate, well-sourced (Stein 1999 AMDIS) explanation of component deconvolution as detection.

assertions.text: The Common Errors fix for 'No GC-MS option in MS-DIAL 5' (use a MS-DIAL 4 build) is the researcher's best available path
assertions.note: Misleading: the researcher's already-installed 5.x console has a working gcms mode; the Skill sends them to source and maintain a separate older build unnecessarily.

assertions.text: Skill correctly recommends retention-index (not raw RT) alignment for GC-EI cross-run comparability
assertions.note: Accurate and well-justified (column-aging RT drift rationale).

inputs.label: Parse an existing AlignResult.txt into pandas and map annotation tags to MSI levels
inputs.note: Python import section runs correctly; the natural Python port of the R-only MS/MS-support check silently fails because pandas auto-casts the export's TRUE/FALSE text to bool.

assertions.text: Python import code (verbatim from SKILL.md) correctly separates metadata from sample intensity columns on a real 4-header-row export
assertions.note: Executed: 30/30 rows and 6/6 sample columns recovered exactly, matching synthetic ground truth.

assertions.text: The Skill's documented MS/MS-support check correctly flags Metabolite/Lipid+MS/MS features as MSI Level 2 when applied via the Python import path the Skill also documents
assertions.note: Executed: pandas.read_csv silently casts the 'TRUE'/'FALSE' text column to native bool dtype, so the `== 'TRUE'` string-comparison idiom (the only idiom SKILL.md gives, in R) evaluates to all-False with zero error or warning when ported to Python -- confirmed with an independent 3-line repro. No feature is ever assigned MSI Level 2.

assertions.text: Fill% >= 70 filter in Python keeps only truly-qualifying features
assertions.note: Executed: ground-truth check confirmed TRUE for all 12 retained features (numeric column unaffected by the bool-cast issue).

assertions.text: Output does not fabricate identification beyond what the data supports
assertions.note: No fabrication observed; the numeric Fill% filtering remains honest even though the MSI-level tagging silently degrades.

key_strengths: R and Python import/parsing logic (header-skip, metadata/sample-column split) verified correct against independently-generated synthetic MS-DIAL-style exports, with exact row/column-count ground-truth checks.
Fill%-based honest-filtering logic -- the Skill's stated core value proposition -- verified correct in R against ground truth.
Quantitative thresholds (Fill%, QC CV, D-ratio, blank filter) are traceable to real, correctly-cited published guidance (Broadhurst 2018, Mahieu 2017), not invented numbers.

Correct scope discipline: explicitly defers QC-CV/D-ratio filtering and MNAR-aware imputation to normalization-qc rather than reimplementing them, and warns that single-pipeline findings are candidates, not results.

recommendations.title: Documented MsdialConsoleApp lcmsdda/lcmsdia commands do not exist
recommendations.problem: Every 'Run MS-DIAL Headless' example invokes 'MsdialConsoleApp <lcmsdda|lcmsdia|gcms>', but the installed MS-DIAL 5.5.260820 console binary is MSDIALCUI.exe and its only LC-MS subcommand is 'lcms' -- DDA and DIA are not separate console tokens.
recommendations.root_cause: The command examples were written against an older or different MS-DIAL console CLI naming convention and were never re-verified against a current MS-DIAL 5.x release.
recommendations.fix: Rename every 'MsdialConsoleApp' reference to the real executable, replace 'lcmsdda'/'lcmsdia' with 'lcms', and document that DDA vs DIA is selected inside the -m method/param file rather than via the console token; also fix the binary name in the Version Compatibility self-check instruction itself.

recommendations.title: 'MS-DIAL 5 excludes GC-MS' claim is contradicted by the installed release
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md states twice (a dedicated subsection and a Common Errors row) that MS-DIAL 5-alpha excludes GC-MS and that GC-EI work requires a MS-DIAL 4 build; the installed MS-DIAL 5.5.260820 console ships a fully working 'gcms' subcommand backed by its own MsdialGcMsApi.dll.
recommendations.root_cause: The claim was accurate for the 5-alpha milestone the Skill was written against but was never re-checked against later MS-DIAL 5.x releases that re-added GC-MS support.
recommendations.fix: Re-verify GC-MS support against the currently-recommended MS-DIAL 5.x release and update or scope the exclusion claim (e.g. '5-alpha only, restored in later 5.x builds') so researchers are not sent to source an unnecessary separate MS-DIAL 4 install.

recommendations.title: Silent MSI-level bug when the R filter idiom is ported to Python
recommendations.problem: The 'Filter the Table Honestly' section gives the MS/MS-support check only in R ('== "TRUE"' against a character column). The natural Python port silently evaluates to all-False because pandas.read_csv auto-casts the export's TRUE/FALSE text to native bool -- with no error or warning -- so every feature loses its MSI Level 2 assignment.
recommendations.root_cause: No Python-specific filter snippet exists, leaving readers to port an R string-comparison idiom into a language where the equivalent column is silently a different dtype.
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit Python filter snippet that compares against boolean True (or forces the column to stay textual, e.g. dtype=str on read_csv), and add the TRUE/FALSE auto-bool-cast trap to the Common Errors table.

recommendations.title: No explicit 'When NOT to use' section
recommendations.problem: Human Usability is reduced because scope boundaries (vs. xcms-preprocessing, vs. normalization-qc, vs. metabolite-annotation) must be inferred from the Related Skills list and prose rather than a dedicated section.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md organizes routing information by topic rather than as an explicit inclusion/exclusion boundary list.
recommendations.fix: Add a short 'When NOT to use' section pointing to xcms-preprocessing, lipidomics, metabolite-annotation and normalization-qc with one line each on why.
